method: Read-only production diff/source inspection and stdlib AST/hash checks
source_hash_scope: Exact working source bodies; runtime qualification and publication are separate

resolved_findings.finding: Native binders could enter SQL/COOR before detecting an active borrowed transaction
resolved_findings.resolution: Task plain/nominated entry points and allocation check original owner custody and connection.in_transaction is False before initial native fences. Server checks before ready SQL; gateway repeats after detached replay. No transaction repair/BEGIN probe.

resolved_findings.finding: Allocation's final observation sampled a clock after the task's closing grant check
resolved_findings.resolution: Gateway samples final time outside SERVER after unlocked native checks. Binding-only task _native and allocation _observe receive that sample, avoiding a later supported wall-clock callback before static closing/source/publication checks. Other native clock contracts keep their defaults.

resolved_findings.finding: Post-constructor observations alone could accept replaced candidate inputs
resolved_findings.resolution: Private configure creates the exact candidate under SERVER before retained CAS. Gateway pins candidate/store/CAS/guard/request/limits/registry and canonical owner-bound body; invokes the original input guard and verifies server policy again after replay.

resolved_findings.finding: Native finally paths formerly discovered whichever genuine reader occupied the gateway slot
resolved_findings.resolution: Gateway installs an exact private attempt publication tuple alongside literal reader fields before post-publication assertions. Task/allocation finally consume only that attempt's witness, identity-joined to the gateway publication record; replacing the current reader does not make the replacement adoptable.

reviewed_properties: Public CurrentSourceLookup construction retains configure then complete-source/replay/subset/full-source order. Private _binding_candidate configures without retained CAS; _replay_binding performs the original replay checks.
Known task/server/gateway SERVER acquisitions end before candidate replay. Actual task/allocation COOR fences run in unlocked checks; closing locked checks enter no COOR or retained CAS.

Gateway bind/read share a short-held busy mutex. Original ticket/check tuple identity is checked; teardown clears only its own active bind ticket. Native task/allocation serialization and consumed-state guards remain.

Canonical server configuration is deeply detached; original server/gateway/connection/identity/config/transport/vault objects remain joined. Candidate owner/body and empty cursor/read state must match before and after callbacks.
Closing binding-specific native grant/task/allocation checks precede complete committed-source validation, including omitted paths. Static owner/candidate checks then precede literal publication.

Prepublication failure publishes nothing and releases only attempt guards, allowing a repaired public retry. Own publication followed by failure retains exact consumed task/allocation/nomination joins; no alternate-reader discovery, clearing or rebind fallback.
Existing public binding and source.get response/cursor contracts remain. Binding creates no proxy grant, worker endpoint, descriptor, process, new CAS or replacement native database.
finite_assumptions_and_limits: The reviewed gateway path and known wrappers release their own SERVER acquisitions. A caller adding an outer SERVER recursion is outside this finite claim; the implementation does not unlock arbitrary caller-owned recursion.

Task/allocation RLocks remain held over the operation. Same-thread native observer callbacks are supported by their existing reentry rules; arbitrary callback-created threads waiting on those locks are not claimed nonblocking.

Only the binding closing clock is detached through the new checked-time parameters. Readiness transport, ordinary native fences/default clocks and arbitrary replaced Python methods are not covered by a universal callback-safety claim.
Physical/source/native checks are sequential observations, not a filesystem writer lease or atomic transaction over Git, COOR, grant memory and filesystem state.

Host fixtures and authored listener/deployment metadata do not qualify deployed worker UID access, cross-process permission handoff, coding-child adoption, signed compiled context, proof execution or official-task completion.
This review does not attest a complete import closure, learned IR reconstruction, changed checkpoints/embeddings, model gains, complete model usage or token savings.
